_note: What `goalcup-verify crates/goalcup-verifier/tests/fixtures/compliant` says with NO flags. The fixture's claim has always been the pass path, and it still is — but the pass path now needs `--dev`, because this trace signs with a seed published in this repository. This file records the reading a plain run gets; `tests/compliant.rs` asserts both halves.
_why_this_file_exists_at_all: It did not until the 2026-09-05 fix wave, and `scripts/regen-compliant-fixture.md` argued against one: a per-code expectation file lets a fixture that stopped exercising a rule keep passing, and this fixture's claim is one sentence. That argument still holds for the PASS claim, which is why `tests/compliant.rs` keeps asserting it in full — every check `pass`, the queue empty, exit 0 — under `--dev`. This file records the other half, which is not a per-code expectation of a passing run but the single Flag a default run raises, and it exists so that Flag cannot change without a diff.
_this_file_is_not_generated: `GOALCUP_REGEN=1 … regenerate` writes the seven files in `support::compliant::FILES` and does not touch this one. It is written from a real run and read by eye, like the adversarial fixture's.
_cause_placeholder_server_key: V13, x1, Flag. `SERVER_PUBLIC_KEYS` holds exactly one entry, `PLACEHOLDER_SERVER_PUBLIC_KEY`, and its private seed is `[5u8; 32]` — written in `tests/support/compliant.rs` so the fixtures can sign a receipt and an acknowledgement at all. Anybody holding this repository can therefore mint a receipt or an ack that resolves to `key_source: "pinned"`, which is the strongest provenance a verdict has. V13 raises this Flag whenever that key is what verified something, so a `pinned` reading can never be mistaken for an anchored one. Replacing the constant with the real organiser key is the release gate before any entry is judged; `--dev` suppresses the Flag in the meantime, because signing with the published seed is the expected thing to do while developing.
_nothing_else_is_in_the_queue: One entry, and it is about the KEY rather than about the run. Every one of the thirteen checks except V13 is `pass` here and V13's own other findings are Pass-level (`binding_checked`), which is the whole point of the fixture: a run that broke no rule reads as a run that broke no rule, and the one thing the verifier will not do is call a signature under a published seed an anchor.
_server_key_unpinned_is_absent: The other half of the same fix-wave finding, and it does not fire here. `server_key_unpinned` is what a key this build does NOT pin raises — `--dev-key`, `--dev-descriptor-key` — and this trace's key is pinned. That is exactly the problem `placeholder_server_key` exists to state: the two codes are complementary, not alternatives.
